hints: Look carefully at the functional groups first, what type of alcohol is on the left and what type of carbonyl is on the right?
Remember that butan-2-one is a methyl ketone with a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so think about what the iodoform test will do to each compound.
Check whether acidified dichromate can oxidise either a tertiary alcohol or a ketone, and contrast that with how 2,4-DNPH behaves toward a carbonyl.
walkthrough:
**Identify the two compounds**

Great start, let's read the skeletons. The left molecule is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(OH)(CH}_3)_2$, which is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol.

The right molecule is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$, which is butan-2-one, a ketone.

**Test 1, alkaline iodine**

This is the iodoform test for the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group and for $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO-R + 3I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{RCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Butan-2-one is a methyl ketone, so it gives a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$. The tertiary alcohol cannot react, so no precipitate. Test 1 distinguishes them.

**Test 2, acidified dichromate**

Acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is an oxidising agent that turns from orange to green when oxidation occurs.

Tertiary alcohols resist oxidation because there is no H on the carbon bearing the $\text{OH}$. Ketones also resist further oxidation under these conditions. Both stay orange, so test 2 cannot distinguish them.

**Test 3, 2,4-DNPH**

2,4-DNPH gives a bright orange precipitate with any aldehyde or ketone, but no reaction with alcohols.

$$\text{R}_2\text{C=O + 2,4-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange hydrazone precipitate + H}_2\text{O}$$
Butan-2-one gives the orange solid, the tertiary alcohol gives nothing. Test 3 distinguishes them. So only 1 and 3 work.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes test 2. Both the tertiary alcohol and the ketone are resistant to oxidation, so acidified dichromate stays orange for both and gives no distinction.
options.B: Correct. Test 1 works because only butan-2-one (methyl ketone) gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline $\text{I}_2$. Test 3 works because only butan-2-one (carbonyl) gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. Test 2 fails for both.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes test 2 and omits test 1. Test 2 fails since neither compound is oxidised, while test 1 is a valid distinction that should be included.
options.D: Incorrect. Test 2 alone cannot distinguish them because there is no colour change with either compound. This choice misses the two tests that do give a positive result with only the ketone.
